question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{2}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{e}^{x+y}]_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}({e}^{y+2}-{e}^{y+1})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}({e}^{y+2}-{e}^{y+1})\text{d}y & =[{e}^{y+2}-{e}^{y+1}]_{1}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{4}-{e}^{3}-({e}^{3}-{e}^{2}) \\  & ={e}^{4}-2{e}^{3}+{e}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
